solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brushing up on foreign language, improving appearance in table?

definitions.meaning: polishing your French, read as a phrase, is improving your command of that language
the furniture finish of shellac rubbed into wood gives a table a glossy look

explanation.surface: Someone revising a foreign tongue, set beside the shine on a dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the phrase into two words: polishing (brushing up) your French.
explanation.definitionFit: The finishing technique of rubbing shellac into wood brings up a high gloss on furniture, while polishing a language means refining it.

clue.text: France needs taller rugby player

parts.note: F is the international code for France
lanker means taller and thinner

explanation.surface: The French side needs a taller man in the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing forward in rugby union, playing on the side of the scrum, is so named.

clue.text: Model can then charm

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape, so the letters of can then are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fashion model can then turn on the charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun, the person charming, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight or captivate someone, as if by a spell, is to charm them.

clue.text: One or two perhaps count in conclave

definitions.meaning: one and two are numbers used for counting, as opposed to ordinal first and second
the papal conclave is made up of cardinals, so their headcount is the number of them

explanation.surface: Tallying how many churchmen are shut in to elect a pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers such as one, two, three are so called, and the phrase also reads as the tally of princes of the Church.

clue.text: One's detained someone snooping around boy

definitions.note: one's detained reads as one who is detained, a noun phrase

indicators.note: around says the snoop's letters surround those for boy

parts.note: a prier is someone who pries, snooping
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone is held after spying around a lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A person held in custody or captivity is the one locked up.

clue.text: Lots let off at first when one's accepted clemency

indicators.note: accepted says the numeral is taken into the shortened word
let off at first says the opening letter is released from the word for lots

parts.note: plenty means lots
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Lots of people are let off at the start when mercy is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let off' suggests the mercy theme, but it removes the P of PLENTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildness or mercy in judging others is a synonym for clemency.

clue.text: First US pilot is somehow crossing over in this

definitions.text: First US pilot is somehow crossing over in this

indicators.note: crossing says those rearranged letters straddle the letter for over
somehow says the letters of first US pilot is fall into some new order

parts.note: O is over in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: The first American airman made the crossing over the Atlantic in this.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lindbergh made the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 1927 in this plane, so the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lindbergh's monoplane, named after the city of his backers, carried him across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Things I worked out?

indicators.note: worked out says the letters of things I are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A list of things someone has figured out for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: understanding is what you have worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep understanding, perceiving what lies beneath, is the product of things one has figured out.

clue.text: Wide-ranging groups of organisms by lake

parts.note: genera are classification groups of related species

explanation.surface: A broad survey of families of species living beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad and not specific, covering many cases, means wide-ranging.

clue.text: Performance dropping tango for string instrument

indicators.note: dropping says the letter for tango leaves the word for performance
for says the string synonym takes the place of the dropped letter

parts.note: a performance is an action, something done
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
cord is thin string

explanation.surface: A musical performance that abandons the tango in favour of a string instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'string instrument' reads as one phrase, but 'string' is wordplay: 'dropping' T and putting CORD 'for' it turns ACTION into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The squeezebox with bellows and keys is a musical instrument, though not a stringed one.

clue.text: Playwright with digestive condition needing nurse

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A dramatist with a stomach complaint who needs medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: EN, an enrolled nurse, is a junior grade of British nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik, the Norwegian author of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler, was a dramatist.

clue.text: Sounds like what you need to drive off in military style

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase for the ignition key is spoken, giving the answer

parts.words: what you need to drive off
parts.note: you need the key to a car before you can drive away

explanation.surface: A riddle about what a driver must have, dressed as a fashion note.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, 'car key' runs together into the two syllables of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dull brownish-yellow cloth and colour is the classic look of army uniforms.

clue.text: Dark Blues set off in racing boat

parts.note: dark blue is Oxford's colour, so the Dark Blues are Oxford University, OU
to set off something is to trigger it

explanation.surface: Oxford's crew launches itself in a racing shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race pits Oxford, the Dark Blues, against Cambridge, the Light Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: A light racing rowing boat with the rowlocks on brackets projecting beyond the hull is so named.

clue.text: Does perhaps cut across vehicle going over repeated route

indicators.note: going over says the whole assembly is turned around
cut across says the animals straddle the vehicle, one each side

parts.note: does, female deer, are an example of deer
a cart is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Female deer cut in front of a vehicle on a road it has driven before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe. 'going over' turns around DECARTER, the result of 'cut across'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have gone back over a path is to have repeated one's route.

clue.text: Lethal weapon finally changes hands

indicators.note: finally changes hands says the last letter swaps from right, R, to left, L

parts.note: a mortar is a short-barrelled gun

explanation.surface: A deadly weapon is at last passed to a new owner.
explanation.walkthrough: R and L stand for right and left hands, so the last R becomes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly wound or blow is called fatal in this sense, causing death.

clue.text: Loose woman cycling I love, being ladies' man

indicators.note: cycling says letters move round from the front of the word to its back

parts.note: a harlot is a loose woman
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A man boasts of loving a promiscuous woman while out on his bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves HAR to the end, giving LOTHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The seducer in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent gave his name to any womaniser.

clue.text: Lots of pipes providing note backing crooner

indicators.note: backing says the note is written backwards

parts.note: ut is the old name for the note doh
Bing Crosby was the famous crooner

explanation.surface: A musical note providing the backing track for a crooner's song.
explanation.walkthrough: UT is the original name of the first note of the scale, now doh.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of hose or tube collectively make a mass noun for a quantity of pipes.

clue.text: Broadcasting to millions consuming little electricity

indicators.note: consuming says the first pair of words swallows the short form

parts.note: elec is a short form of electricity

explanation.surface: Transmitting to millions of viewers while using hardly any power.
explanation.definitionFit: Communication by cable, radio or broadcasting over distance is the field this shortened word names.

clue.text: Brand of wine to get sister down? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse says the two words come in the opposite order to the phrase just described

parts.note: blue means down, depressed
a nun is a sister in a religious order

explanation.surface: A glass of wine to cheer up a gloomy nun, or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: To get sister down is to make a NUN BLUE; 'The reverse' swaps the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A German Liebfraumilch sold under this label is a well-known brand of wine.

clue.text: Spies dog out of control — was rabbiting

indicators.note: out of control says the letters of spies dog run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Agents trail a target in chaos while someone chatters away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbiting' is British slang for chattering on, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattering idly, especially about other people's affairs, is the sense shared by the slang verb.

clue.text: Criticise expert over a wonder cure

indicators.note: over says in this down clue that the earlier pieces sit above the letter a

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Knocking an expert who boasts of a miracle remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposed remedy for all ills is a miracle cure.

clue.text: Takes risks besieging old eastern bishop's territory

indicators.note: besieging says the risk-taking word surrounds the letter for old

parts.note: dices, as in dices with death, means takes risks

explanation.surface: Daredevils lay siege to the old eastern lands of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The district under a bishop's pastoral care is his see, an area of church administration.

clue.text: Hippopotamus clearly shows strength

indicators.note: shows says the run of letters is on display inside hippopotamus clearly

explanation.surface: A hippo plainly displays great physical power.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn or physical power, as in having the muscle to do something.

clue.text: Showy insect flying round university — one makes a lot of noise

definitions.text: one makes a lot of noise

parts.note: loud colours are showy and garish

indicators.note: flying round says the insect circles the university letter

parts.note: a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: A gaudy insect flutters around a campus, making a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who talks too much and too noisily is a braggart making a lot of noise.

clue.text: Tongue and groove primarily used in flooring

indicators.note: used in says that letter is set inside the floor covering

parts.note: lino, linoleum, is a floor covering

indicators.note: primarily says only the opening letter of groove is taken

explanation.surface: Tongue-and-groove joints are mainly what floors are fitted with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue and groove' reads as a carpentry joint, but 'Tongue' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for a language, especially a foreign or specialist one, a tongue.

clue.text: An Olympic medallist going round in small boat

indicators.note: going round says the athlete's name encircles the word an

parts.note: Sebastian Coe won Olympic golds at 1500 metres

explanation.surface: An Olympic medallist paddling around in a little craft.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is a British middle-distance runner, double Olympic 1500m champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A light narrow vessel paddled by hand is a small boat.

clue.text: Fattening food's given relative inflammation

parts.note: carb, short for carbohydrate, is reputedly fattening food
an uncle is a relative

explanation.surface: Starchy food given to a relative brings on a nasty swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cluster of boils, a painful infected swelling of the skin, is a form of inflammation.

clue.text: Trite manifesto's concocted by member of government

indicators.note: concocted says the letters of trite manifesto's are cooked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A government member has cobbled together a banal election manifesto.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a junior minister below cabinet rank holds this title in a government department.
